subject: Connector interoperability: cold-tier policies & partner data contracts

Subject: Connector interoperability: cold-tier policies & partner data contracts

Hi all —

Thanks for taking time to align on the connector surface. We're kicking off a short cross-partner sync to iron out:

- cold-tiering / object lifecycle expectations when embeddings are offloaded to S3 (TTL, versioning)
- fallthrough behavior when pgvector or managed vector DB is unavailable
- semantics for metadata preservation (visibility to downstream search / filters)
- SLAs and operational contacts for warm/cold retrieval latency targets

Attached is our first-pass connector matrix (connector_matrix_v2.xlsx) with columns for API contract, fallback order, and expected failure modes. Please review the matrix and call out any mismatches by EOD Wednesday PST.

Proposed short outcomes from this thread: 1) Agreed contract for offload/fallback order; 2) Owner for retention/GC policy per partner; 3) A simple canary test plan for decreased availability.

Next steps: can we schedule a 45-min working call this week? I can host on Thursday 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Connector interoperability: cold-tier policies & partner data contracts

Thanks Vivek — good to see this. A few quick clarifying questions from Pinecone side:

1) For the "fallthrough" step you have "pgvector -> S3" as an example. We typically recommend returning cached vectors for up to 24h and doing async backfill to cold storage. Can you confirm whether Redwood expects synchronous reads from S3 in the hot path, or if async is acceptable?

2) On metadata, are you expecting Redwood to preserve full JSON document payload when evicting embeddings, or a minimal pointer (doc_id + checksum)? This affects our restore latency significantly.

3) Regarding access controls: if a customer is on Dedicated, do you expect Pinecone to call back to Redwood's control plane for KMS retrievals, or will the customer provide direct KMS access keys to Pinecone?

Happy to join the call Thursday; 10am PT works for me. I attached a short ops FAQ that maps our recommended best practices.

Cheers,
Andrew Finch
Solutions Engineering, Pinecone
[Attachment: pinecone-ops-faq.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: vivek@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Connector interoperability: cold-tier policies & partner data contracts

Andrew — nice notes. Below are the engineering constraints from our side that will impact the contract choices:

- Synchronous S3 reads in the hot path are allowed only when expected latency <= 250ms P95; otherwise we want an async queue + indirect pointer.
- On eviction we keep a minimal pointer (doc_id, table, checksum, metadata blob pointer) rather than full document JSON to limit object size. Full payloads may be stored behind a "document archive" pointer for compliance retention.
- For Dedicated customers we prefer customer-managed KMS and short-lived credentials for the ingestion path (so the customer retains key ownership). For Hosted customers, Redwood will broker KMS calls with partner vendors under a documented role assumption.

I've annotated connector_matrix_v2.xlsx with these constraints. I'm prepping a tiny canary runner (lambda + synthetic vectors) that will run a restore/evict cycle — target run next Wed.

- Dev
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

We reviewed the matrix and Dev's notes. A couple items from Weaviate's side:

- Weaviate's native backup/restore supports payload preservation but retrieval latency from object stores varies by region and S3 tier; we can offer an "archive pointer" pattern that references object storage and a lightweight metadata header for search.
- For ACLs we can accept role-assumption tokens from Redwood (hosted) or customer-provided credentials for Dedicated. We'll need the KMS flow documented for compliance checks.
- We propose a shared test harness (minimal runner) that executes: ingest -> evict -> read-back -> score parity check. If partners agree, VectorWorks can run the harness in a neutral cloud account and share logs.

Happy to join Thursday 10am PT and walk through our connector behavior.

Cheers,
Sara
Partner Engineering, Weaviate

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: andrew@pinecone.io, sara@weaviate.ai, elena.ruiz@vectorworks.co
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Connector interoperability: cold-tier policies & partner data contracts

Thanks everyone — good alignment so far. Quick summary and asks: 

1) Contract: use "pointer-first" eviction (doc_id + metadata pointer) with optional archive pointer for customers who opt into full payload retention.
2) Hot path: synchronous S3 read allowed only if partners can meet <=250ms P95; otherwise async restore flow with a best-effort warm cache.
3) KMS: Dedicated = customer-provided keys; Hosted = Redwood brokered role assumption (document required).
4) Test harness: agree to Sara's harness; ask VectorWorks to run initial job and publish results to shared drive (link above).

Actions:
- VectorWorks (Elena) to confirm test account and timeline by Mon 12/6.
- Pinecone (Andrew) to confirm whether you can meet the 250ms P95 for the synchronous S3 read for our baseline payload size (16KB).
- Weaviate (Sara) to add ACL/KMS steps to the test plan.
- Dev to share the canary runner repo and an example payload by EOD Monday.

Laura / Grace: please own the operational runbooks and create a simple SLA appendix we can include in partner PSAs. I'll sync with sales on commercial language next week.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
